newsitem.title: USA: US rail carloads, ton-miles up from year ago - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail carloads, ton-miles up from year ago - AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic as measured in carloads and ton-miles rose in the week ended January 4 from the same week a year ago but intermodal fell, the Association of American Railroads said Friday.

The AAR said carloads totaled 294,980 in the January 4 week, up three percent from 286,279 in the first week of 1996. Ton-miles in the week were 22.9 billion, up 4.6 percent from 21.9 billion a year ago.
A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.
But intermodal volume, which does not include carloads, fell 1.2 percent to 114,866 trailers and containers in the week from 116,275 in the year-ago week.

AAR said the biggest carload gains were in farm products excluding grain, up 53.6 percent to 1,702 loadings from 1,108 in the year-ago week, and in metals and related products, up 15 percent to 11,433 carloads from 9,945 a year ago.
Grain mill products also rose 13 percent to 9,722 carloads in the week from 8,601 last year.

AAR said the biggest declines from the year-ago week were in carloads of motor vehicles and equipment, which fell 44.1 percent to 6,237 from 11,160, and in metallic ores, down 16.1 percent to 16,452 carloads from 19,611 a year ago.

AAR also said U.S. rail carloads to Canada, which are counted separately, fell 25.6 percent from a year ago to 28,435. It said intermodal volume to Canada totaled 14,435 trailers and containers, down two percent from the year-ago week.
